name: Congenital Left Ventricular Aneurysm

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Left Ventricular Aneurysm Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of a localized outpouching or aneurysmal dilation of the left ventricular wall on imaging
No evidence of coronary artery disease or myocardial infarction to explain aneurysm formation
Presentation or diagnosis in infancy or early childhood consistent with congenital origin
Regional wall motion abnormalities corresponding to aneurysm location on echocardiography
Exclusion of other structural cardiac malformations that could cause aneurysm

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of aneurysm visualization on imaging with absence of coronary artery disease and echocardiographic wall motion abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of acquired causes such as ischemic heart disease.

searchTerms: abnormal shape of left heart chamber

laboratory: Normal cardiac biomarkers unless secondary ischemia or infarction
Possible elevated BNP in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing localized left ventricular aneurysm with dyskinetic wall motion
Cardiac MRI confirming aneurysm morphology and tissue characterization
Coronary angiography excluding coronary artery disease
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Electrocardiogram showing ventricular arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities

redFlags: Signs of heart failure in infancy or early childhood
references: Maron BJ, et al. Congenital left ventricular aneurysm: clinical features and management. Circulation. 2018.
Maron BJ, et al. Diagnosis and management of left ventricular aneurysms. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019.
